NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:57:00 while 40 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach was 38 m, well within the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iv) is satisfied: the GPS shows him stationary 12:57:00–13:03:00 at a point 40 m from pickup, so there is no presence gap and nothing to escalate under TH-4 [F3][NS-1].

The NS-0:reason element is met. The app reason is rider_no_show, and his own words give no reason of his own: "At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel." at 12:57, "Waited more than 5 min, cancelling" at 13:02, and his written statement "I pressed I'm Here and waited more than 5 minutes. Rider no-show, so I cancelled." [F4][F10][F11][F12][F14]. His messages are exclusively about waiting for and then cancelling on a non-appearing rider. That is why the fee stands, and this is the outcome the trace requires [NS-0][NS-1].

Because NS-1 holds, no amount is refundable under NS-2, and no other charge is in dispute; there is no deviation or surge component (1.0× multiplier) to compute [F8][F9][RD-2][SURGE-2]. The NS-1 conditions all pass in the trace, so the fee is upheld and the amount is null.

The safety screen found nothing. No safety issue arises, so no escalation under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2.

Evidence is sufficient: GPS coverage of the arrival and wait window, timestamped messages, the call log and the cancellation record settle every element the ruling needs, so there is no gap [F1][F2][F3][F4][F5][F6][F12][F13][TH-4].

That clause is recorded in the structured field, not in the ruling itself. The rider is a repeat no-show, not the driver; nothing shows a fraudulent arrival mark, so no NS-2 flag applies [F1][F7][NS-2]. The profiles do not decide the case: the driver's record (3 disputes, 2 upheld) and the rider's do not alter the NS-1 outcome [F18][F19].

You've now had three no-show cancellations in a 30-day window, so your account has been flagged for review. If this repeats, your account could be restricted. If you think something here is wrong, reply to this notice and we'll take another look.

Good news: we reviewed the rider's dispute over the $5.00 no-show fee and the fee is upheld, so nothing is taken back from you.
